api:
OV.DogfightUI = {
  open(G, dogfightId?, opts?) -> bool   pushes scene 'dogfight' (isScreen:false) or adds a panel to the open overlay; with no id it adopts every G.dogfights entry that has no panel yet. opts (from the first call, or per panel):
      onEnd(summary)              called once per dogfight when its panel closes
      onEvents(events, summary)   campaign events created by Dogfight.finish (ufoCrashed/ufoDestroyed/ufoEscaped/craftLost/dogfightEnd…), spliced out of G.events tick by tick. With no handler they are pushed back into G.events in order at panel close, so GeoUI's next drain shows them.
      onClose(summaries)          when the last panel closes and the scene leaves
  close(dogfightId?) -> bool       closes a panel now (all of them with no id); a dogfight still running is ended with OV.Dogfight.finish (outcome 'disengaged')
  minimise(dogfightId?) ; restore(dogfightId?) ; toggle(dogfightId?)   with no id: the focused or most recent panel. One panel is expanded at a time; the others are chips in .df-dock (bottom-left; CSS vars --df-dock-left / --df-dock-bottom let GeoUI move it)
  active() -> [{dogfightId, craftId, ufoId, minimised, over, outcome}] ; isOpen(dogfightId?) -> bool
  isPaused() -> bool ; setPaused(bool, quiet?)   quiet = no «Pausa» overlay and no sound (for screenshots, or a popup above)
  model: { ticksFor(acc, dt, tickMs, max)->{n, acc}, newTrack(G,d), absorb(track,G,d,tickEvents), absorbGeo(track,campaignEvents), status(G,d,track)->{key,params,tone,warn}, weaponInfo(G,d,slot,track), summary(track), outcomeTone, apparentR(ufoType,dist), depthK(z), craftLabel(G,craft), ufoLabel(G,ufo), SHAPES, MAX_TICKS:8, OUTCOME_MS:2400 }   pure, no DOM, tested in Node
}
summary = {dogfightId, craftId, ufoId, craftType, ufoType, outcome, seaCrash, titleKey, tone, subs:[{key,params}], shots, hits, dealt, taken, ufoShots, ufoHits, ticks, seconds, craftHp, craftMaxHp, ufoDmgPct, events}
Scene: OV.SceneDefs.dogfight({G, dogfightIds:[id], opts?}). On exit it calls OV.Scenes.pop({dogfight: summaries}), so the scene below receives it in resume(result). If another scene sits on top when the last panel closes, the pop is deferred until the overlay is top again. If the scene is torn down by Scenes.set, running dogfights are finished as 'disengaged' and their events delivered.
Loop: think(dt) runs OV.Dogfight.tick once per Data.dogfight.tickMs of real time, up to 8 ticks per frame, for every running panel (minimised panels keep fighting). It is independent of globe speed. It stops for P/Space, for any OV.Dom modal, for another scene on top, and auto-pauses on onHidden.
Input: keys 1–5 set posture, Q/E toggle weapon 1/2, M toggles minimise, Esc minimises, Tab cycles dogfights, P/Space pauses, Enter closes a result. When everything is minimised, the camera gestures (hover/drag/pan/zoom/wheel/dblclick, arrows, +/−) are forwarded to the scene below; clicks are not.
i18n: df.* keys, including df.start ('Contacto! {craft} interceta {ufo}') and df.end.<outcome> plus df.end.seaCrash / df.end.damaged, ready for Geoscape toasts.
summary:
The interception overlay is built and has been through 3 screenshot-and-fix rounds in Chromium at 1440×900, 1024×700 and iPad touch. The QA script passes all 42 of its checks. The 7 new Node tests pass. The full `--strict` suite gives 533 passed and 1 failed; the failure is not in my files (see open issues).

**How it plays**
- It is a compact framed panel over the Geoscape (canvas plus DOM), with the battle HUD's look: amber accent, the base.css tokens and the OV.Dom helpers.
- **Canvas view**:
  - The sky depends on the UFO's altitude and on day, dusk or night at its position. Below it is land or sea, and the horizon curves at high altitude.
  - Clouds stream past at the closing speed, and the view banks when you change posture.
  - Each UFO type has its own 3/4 silhouette with spinning rim lights. It grows in true perspective as the distance closes. It smokes and burns as damage builds.
  - Weapons: Stingray/Avalanche missiles fly with flame, a motion streak and smoke trails. Cannon fire shows as tracers. Laser and plasma show as beams. UFO plasma bolts fly toward the camera.
  - Feedback: explosions, flashes, camera shake, a red vignette when the craft is hit, floating damage numbers and «falhou» on misses.
  - HUD: gunsight, pitch ladder, and target brackets that switch from «A SEGUIR» to «NA MIRA» when a live weapon is in range.
- **Range bar**: distance from 0 to 800 with a mark for each weapon's range, the UFO weapon zone hatched in red (or «OVNI desarmado»), the safe-distance line, the posture's target as a triangle, and a UFO marker that pulses when you are under fire.
- **Controls**: five posture buttons (keys 1–5, current one highlighted, all locked while the UFO is outrunning the craft). Hull bar for the craft, UFO damage % with a 50 % «queda» mark. Each weapon card shows ammo pips or count, hit %, range, a reload/state bar and an on/off toggle (Q/E). Every button has a tooltip naming its shortcut.
- **Status lines**: approaching, in range, holding, safe distance with a hint to press 2–4, retreating, disengaging, UFO fleeing, out of ammo, plus warnings for being under fire, the Cautious auto-retreat and the UFO breaking off.
- **Endings**:
  - Each outcome has its own animation: the UFO falls with smoke, explodes, streaks away, or slides off as the craft turns. If the craft is lost, the glass cracks and the view fades to static.
  - Then a banner: «OVNI despenhado», «OVNI destruído» (also when it crashes into the sea), «OVNI escapou», «Nave danificada», «Nave destruída», and also «Interceção interrompida» and «Sem munições».
  - The banner shows shots, hits, damage dealt and taken, and duration, with a «Continuar ↵» button. It closes by itself after 2.4 s.
- **Two dogfights**: one panel is open and the other is a live chip (status, mini hull bars, distance) that flashes when hit. A minimised fight that ends reopens to show its result.
- **Sound** comes from the existing `OV.audio` effects. The «interception» music and a «dogfight_engine» effect are used if the audio module ever adds them.

**QA** (`qa/dogfight_check.mjs`) builds G with `OV.Campaign.newCampaign`, puts a UFO in the air and reaches contact with `OV.World.launch` and `World.step`. The second simultaneous fight uses `OV.Dogfight.create`. The overlay opens over the menu; the Geoscape scene is detected if present. It plays every posture, toggles weapons, pauses, disengages, and runs an escape (Abductor), a craft loss (Battleship), two dogfights with minimise and Tab, and `close()`. It checks event delivery, that G.dogfights is empty afterwards, that saving works again, panel fit at 1024×700, and touch targets ≥ 32 px. It also fails on console errors and missing ⟦keys⟧. Screenshots are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-HelloWorld/b8cfbac1-629a-5f58-8dfb-0f752cc84b7c/scratchpad/ui4/dogfight/.

**What the rounds fixed**
1. **Round 1**: bigger UFO scale per size class, the HUD label overlapping the distance, hit % showing 0 after the end, a shorter chip status, and a stronger banner backdrop. The QA timing was also wrong: 2× screenshots are slower than the auto-close, so the script now freezes the fight in the frame where the event happens.
2. **Round 2**: the status text no longer shows under the banner.
3. **Round 3**: missiles were hard to see, so they now have a streak, a bigger flame and a denser trail.

In headless Chromium at 2×, drawing the canvas takes a median of 1.2 ms per frame.
deviations: The result shows for 2.4 s after a 0.65–0.9 s ending animation (contract §6.4 says 1.5 s). The longer time lets the summary be read; Enter or «Continuar» closes it at once.

Minimise is allowed in any posture (the original allows it only at Distância), and a minimised dogfight keeps fighting. The Geoscape stays paused anyway, because World.step refuses to run while dogfights exist.

The UFO type name is shown only if the UFO is hyper-wave identified or its type is in G.seen.ufoTypes; otherwise the size class is shown («OVNI-3 · Pequeno»). The per-type silhouette is always drawn, as the original shows the UFO graphic.
The «Nave danificada» banner replaces «OVNI escapou», «Interceção interrompida» or «Sem munições» when the craft survives with 50 % hull or less. The original outcome becomes the subtitle.

Campaign events from Dogfight.finish are spliced out of G.events after each tick and handed over when the panel closes, through opts.onEvents, or pushed back into G.events if no handler is given. This keeps Geoscape popups from opening on top of the result animation.

No engine loop or interception music exists in OV.audio. Both are feature-detected ('dogfight_engine' effect, 'interception' mood), and the existing effects stand in: dogfight_missile, dogfight_cannon, laser, plasma, dogfight_hit, explosion_small/large, ufo_crash, radar_ping, reaction_alert, ui_*.
open_issues: The one `--strict` failure is not in my files: tools/tests/data_geo.test.js › «raças por mês (ours) e terror com Homens-Serpente» expects {snakeman:60, floater:20, sectoid:20} but gets {floater:70, sectoid:30}. This matches an in-progress raceSchedule edit by another engineer in js/data/geo.js (it is git-modified, and the World engineer had suggested this exact change). The data and its test need to be brought back in line by their owners.

Geoscape engineer, integration: on `dogfightStart`, call `OV.DogfightUI.open(G, ev.dogfightId, {onEvents: handle})` with the same handler you use for the World.step drain. Keep handling `dogfightEnd` only as a toast (`df.end.<outcome>` keys exist). If you need the results, they arrive in your scene's `resume(result)` as `result.dogfight`. If the chips collide with your HUD, set `--df-dock-left` / `--df-dock-bottom` on `.df-dock`. When you push a popup above the overlay, the dogfight freezes automatically.

Audio owner: please add an 'interception' music mood (tense, fast) and a short 'dogfight_engine' effect (jet rumble about 1.5 s, played every 1.7 s while a fight is open). The overlay already picks both up when present.

Balance, for the lead (sim, not UI): at Veterano and above, a Battleship one-shots an Interceptor (power 140 vs 100 HP) from 520 away. That is faithful to the original but brutal. Small Scouts are often destroyed outright (hp 50 vs Stingray 35–70), which leaves no crash site; the UI explains this with «nada a recuperar, mas a pontuação é dobrada». Switching the Stingray off (Q) to bring it down with the cannon is the in-game counter, and the new range bar and hit % make that readable.
